findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok cards and their "Best hostels >" lines, which the hero's "Explore destinations" button scrolls to
findings.fault: The page's second job is to send visitors on to the destination guides, and that path ends here. The cards and their "Best hostels" lines look like links, but parts.txt lists all three as static, so a click does nothing. A visitor follows "Explore destinations" and then has nowhere to go.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next hop. They came for hostels in Canggu or Uluwatu, tap the guide, get nothing back, and decide the site is broken or empty.

findings.where: "How we rank" in the top nav and the footer
findings.fault: The hero's one reason to care is a search that ranks hostels "on merit alone". The link that should back that up goes to this same page, so the claim has no method behind it. The product's own principle is that ranking methods are published.
findings.who_objects: A traveller wary of OTA rankings that partners pay for. They click to check what "merit" means, land back where they started, and read the claim as marketing.

findings.where: Hero, the coral "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news" button
findings.fault: Signing up means writing an email from scratch. Nothing says what to write, what launch news they will get, how often, or that the address won't be used for anything else. On a phone the button can also open no mail app at all. The label leads with an email address, not with what the visitor gets.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone, often in transit on a weak connection. Writing an email to a stranger costs more than a one-field sign-up, and with no promise about use, many won't hand over their address.

findings.where: Hero, first screen: the eyebrow "The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.", the h1 "MantaHostels" and the small body copy under it
findings.fault: The largest text is only the brand name. The promise is a vague "better way" in the eyebrow, with no reason given. The concrete reasons to care (merit-only ranking, booking direct or through your usual site) sit in the smallest type in the hero. The backpacker it is for is never named, so in 5 seconds a reader gets the name, not the benefit.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning quickly. They see a logo and an empty "better". The brand's own rule says the loud half should be a claim with plain mechanics beneath it, but here the loud half is just the name.

findings.where: The whole page, especially the hero and the "Where we're starting" cards
findings.fault: Nothing on the page backs up the pitch. The project holds real facts it could show, such as 172 confirmed hostels mapped across 23 locations, but the destination cards give only a place name. The page asks for trust with nothing to show for it.
findings.who_objects: A traveller deciding whether a pre-launch site is worth an email. With no checkable fact, it looks like a placeholder, not a product being built.

findings.fault: All three link to this same page. A visitor about to send their email address who checks the privacy terms finds there are none.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor, especially from the EU or UK. They expect to see how their address will be handled before they share it, and a dead privacy link reads as careless or evasive.

findings.where: "Where we're starting" cards: monospace type, purple borders, heavy drop shadows
findings.fault: The cards look like an unstyled developer template, out of step with the beachy hero and footer around them. The page reads as unfinished, which works against a brand whose product is trust and whose named enemy is the sterile look.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor sizing up a site they have never heard of. A half-built-looking section makes them doubt whether the product, and the launch news, are real.

findings.where: Footer line "Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali" against the "Where we're starting" card for Kuta Lombok
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali, but the starting destinations above include Lombok. The page contradicts itself about where Manta works now.
findings.who_objects: A traveller headed to Lombok. They can't tell whether that guide is live or whether the footer is out of date, and small contradictions chip at credibility.

findings.where: Hero CTA and footer: the only sign of who is behind the site is the address luc@mantahostels.com
findings.fault: The visitor is asked to email "luc", but the page never says who Luc is or that one founder is building this.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to write to an unknown person. A one-line "who's building this" would turn an anonymous address into a person they can trust with an email.
